source_text: Engagement of the fusion peptide with a target membrane requires formation of an extended intermediate to project it beyond the outer margin of adjacent HA1 heads
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from structural knowledge of HA and geometric constraints.

claim: For an extended intermediate to form, the HA1 heads must dissociate from their contact with an HA2 loop (HA2 residues 58–74).
source_text: For an intermediate to form that resembles the inner core of the ultimate, low-pH triggered structure (as drawn for the extended structure in Figure 1A), the HA1 heads must dissociate from their contact with an HA2 loop (HA2 residues 58–74: see Figure 3D) between the short first α-helix (HA2, residues 38–57) and the long central α-helix (HA2, residues 75–127)
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from structural knowledge cited from Godley et al., 1992.

claim: The HA2 loop (residues 58–74) must reverse direction and become itself a helix during formation of the extended intermediate.
source_text: and that loop must in turn reverse direction and become itself a helix
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from structural knowledge of the pre- and post-fusion conformations.

claim: Extension of the central trimeric coiled-coil probably drives the loop-to-helix conversion.
source_text: Extension of the central trimeric coiled-coil probably drives the latter process
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from structural considerations cited from Carr and Kim, 1993.

claim: The amino-acid sequence of the HA2 loop strongly favors a helical conformation.
source_text: as the amino-acid sequence of the loop strongly favors such a conformation

claim: Additional necessary structural changes include dissociation of two strands (HA2, residues 21–38) from the edge of the small β-sheet near the base of the HA trimer.
source_text: Further necessary structural changes, in addition to release of the fusion peptide from its pocket, are dissociation of two strands (HA2, residues 21–38) from the edge of the small β-sheet near the base of the HA trimer
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from structural knowledge of HA conformational changes.

claim: The extended intermediate would project the fusion peptide no more than about 25 Å beyond the palisade of un-triggered HAs.
source_text: The structure thus pictured would project the fusion peptide no more than about 25 Å beyond the palisade of un-triggered HAs
evidence_reasoning: This is estimated from structural considerations and geometric calculations.

claim: The intermediate that mediates arrest and hemifusion must be almost completely extended, at least for part of its lifetime.
source_text: In short, the intermediate that mediates arrest and hemifusion must indeed be almost completely extended, at least for part of its lifetime.
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the structural constraints and the experimental observations.

claim: The structures of the initial and final states do not dictate a unique ordering of the conformational change events.
source_text: The structures of the initial and final states do not dictate a unique ordering of the events just listed
evidence_reasoning: This is based on structural knowledge and the fact that multiple pathways are possible.

claim: Breaking the interactions that restrain the fusion peptide is rate-limiting both for virion arrest and for hemifusion at the pH of endosomes (approximately 5 to 5.5).
source_text: Our results show that breaking the interactions that restrain the fusion peptide is rate-limiting both for virion arrest and for hemifusion at the pH of endosomes from which influenza virus penetrates (approximately 5 to 5.5)
evidence_reasoning: This is concluded from the mutation effects on kinetics at physiological pH.

claim: The rate-limiting nature of fusion-peptide release is consistent with the dominance hierarchy of mutations that influence the threshold pH for fusion.
source_text: this interpretation is consistent with the dominance hierarchy of mutations that influence the threshold pH for fusion
evidence_reasoning: This is consistent with prior work cited from Steinhauer et al., 1996.

claim: Mutations that affect the pH dependence of fusion map to a number of sites distributed across the HA2 trimer interface.
source_text: Mutations that affect the pH dependence of fusion map to a number of sites distributed across the HA2 trimer interface
evidence_reasoning: This is cited from Daniels et al., 1985.

claim: Changes in the stability of the HA2 trimer interface will influence fluctuations from the equilibrium structure and the 'window of opportunity' for the fusion peptide to withdraw productively from its pocket.
source_text: Changes in the stability of this interface will influence fluctuations from the equilibrium structure and hence the 'window of opportunity' for the fusion peptide to withdraw productively from its pocket.
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from understanding of protein dynamics and stability.

claim: Emergence of the fusion peptide can in principle precede other conformational events, which then must follow rapidly.
source_text: Emergence of the fusion peptide can in principle precede the other events, which then must follow rapidly (or the peptide will reinsert)
evidence_reasoning: This is a speculative mechanistic possibility based on structural considerations.

claim: Extension of the central coiled-coil by residues 20–74 may exert a 'tug' to extract the fusion peptide.
source_text: perhaps more frequently, extension of the central coiled-coil by residues 20–74 may exert a 'tug' to extract the fusion peptide
evidence_reasoning: This is a speculative mechanistic possibility based on structural considerations.

claim: The fusion-peptide contacts are conserved in all field-isolated influenza HA virions.
source_text: The fusion-peptide contacts, conserved in all field-isolated influenza HA virions
evidence_reasoning: This is based on sequence conservation analysis.

claim: Fusion-peptide contacts form upon cleavage of HA0.
source_text: form upon cleavage of HA0
evidence_reasoning: This is cited from Chen et al., 1998 and Russell et al., 2004.

claim: The stability of fusion-peptide contacts is critical for viral transmission.
source_text: Their stability is critical for viral transmission, not only in the passage from one host or cell to another, but also during entry
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from understanding of the viral life cycle and entry mechanism.

claim: Fusion will be relatively unproductive if it occurs before the pH has dropped enough to allow M2-mediated acidification of the particle interior.
source_text: as fusion will be relatively unproductive if it occurs before the pH of the surrounding compartment has dropped enough to allow M2-mediated acidification of the particle interior
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from understanding of the entry mechanism cited from Ivanovic et al., 2012.

claim: M2-mediated acidification of the particle interior induces dissociation of the eight ribonucleoproteins (RNPs) of the viral genome from the matrix protein, M1.
source_text: which induces dissociation of the eight ribonucleoproteins (RNPs) of the viral genome from the matrix protein, M1
evidence_reasoning: This is cited from Martin and Helenius, 1991.

claim: Fusion too rapid for adequate acidification would release an inactive M1-RNP complex.
source_text: Fusion too rapid for adequate acidification would release an inactive M1-RNP complex.
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from understanding of the requirement for RNP release for productive infection.

claim: Evidence for extended intermediates for other viral fusion proteins is largely indirect.
source_text: Evidence for extended intermediates for other viral fusion proteins is largely indirect.
evidence_reasoning: This is a general statement about the state of knowledge in the field.

claim: The most extensive data for extended intermediates are for HIV gp41.
source_text: The most extensive data are for HIV gp41
evidence_reasoning: This is based on the body of literature on HIV fusion.

claim: Binding of peptides such as C34 and T-20 to HIV gp41 indicates that the inner-core coiled-coil must be present before the outer layer folds back against it.
source_text: in which binding of peptides such as C34 (Chan et al., 1998) and T-20 (Wild et al., 1994), mimics for the outer layer of the final, hairpin structure, indicates that the inner-core coiled-coil must be present before the outer layer folds back against it
evidence_reasoning: This is cited from Chan et al., 1998 and Wild et al., 1994.

claim: Outer-layer peptides from paramyxovirus F proteins similarly inhibit fusion.
source_text: Outer-layer peptides from paramyxovirus F proteins similarly inhibit fusion
evidence_reasoning: This is cited from Lambert et al., 1996.

claim: Electron microscopy of human parainfluenza virus 5 (PIV5) fusing with target vesicles shows a distance between viral and target membranes that corresponds to the gap expected for the putative extended intermediate of F.
source_text: Electron microscopy of human parainfluenza virus 5 (PIV5) fusing with target vesicles shows a distance between viral and target membranes that corresponds to the gap expected for the putative extended intermediate of F
evidence_reasoning: This is cited from Kim et al., 2011.

claim: The HA extended intermediate projects much less far from the viral membrane than does the pre-fusion form, unlike the PIV5 F intermediate.
source_text: which (unlike the HA intermediate) should project much farther from the viral membrane than does the pre-fusion form
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from structural comparisons between HA and F proteins.

claim: The lifetime of an isolated extended HA intermediate is substantial because fusion requires several neighboring HA trimers.
source_text: The relative kinetics of HA-mediated hemifusion and arrest show that because fusion requires several neighboring HA trimers, the lifetime of an isolated extended intermediate is substantial.
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the kinetic data showing different rates for arrest and hemifusion.

claim: The mean lifetime of the 'pioneer' extended HA in any patch can be as long as a minute or more, depending on pH.
source_text: and the mean lifetime of the 'pioneer' extended HA in any patch can be as long as a minute or more, depending on pH
evidence_reasoning: This is calculated from the kinetic data at different pH values.

claim: A relatively long-lived extended intermediate could prove to be a clinically useful target for an influenza-virus entry inhibitor.
source_text: Thus, a relatively long-lived extended intermediate could prove to be a clinically useful target for an influenza-virus entry inhibitor
evidence_reasoning: This is a speculative application of the findings to drug development.

claim: The inherent lower limit to the stability of the pre-fusion HA combined with the requirement for coordinated action of multiple HAs curbs the ability of a virus to escape inhibitor treatment by mutations that accelerate fusion.
source_text: the inherent lower limit to the stability of the pre-fusion HA combined with the requirement for the coordinated action of multiple, independently-triggered HAs to induce fusion, curbs the ability of a virus to escape such treatment by mutations that accelerate fusion-inducing rearrangements
evidence_reasoning: This is a speculative inference about resistance mechanisms based on the findings.

claim: The only clinically approved inhibitor of virus fusion targets the extended intermediate of the HIV fusion protein, gp41.
source_text: The only clinically approved inhibitor of virus fusion targets the extended intermediate of the HIV fusion protein, gp41
evidence_reasoning: This is cited from Wild et al., 1994 and Kilby and Enron, 2003.

claim: Analogous inhibitors have been designed for paramyxoviruses, influenza virus, and flaviviruses.
source_text: analogous inhibitors have been designed for paramyxoviruses (Lambert et al., 1996), influenza virus (Lee et al., 2011) and flaviviruses (Schmidt et al., 2010a, 2010b)
evidence_reasoning: This is cited from multiple sources.

claim: The low surface density of the HIV-envelope protein and the indication that one HIV-envelope trimer may be sufficient to mediate fusion have led to the inference that a single, trimeric gp41 mediates fusion through a very slow fold-back transition.
source_text: the low surface density of the HIV-envelope protein (Chertova et al., 2002; Zhu et al., 2003), and the indication, from experiments with virions bearing mixtures of active and inactive spikes, that one HIV-envelope trimer may be sufficient to mediate fusion (Yang et al., 2005), have led to the inference that a single, trimeric gp41 mediates fusion through a very slow fold-back transition
evidence_reasoning: This is an inference from the field based on multiple cited studies.

claim: There can be a long-lived extended intermediate species even when the fold-back transition itself is fast.
source_text: The data presented here for influenza HA show that there can be a long-lived species, analogous to the extended form of gp41, even when the fold-back transition itself is fast.
evidence_reasoning: This is a key conclusion from the current study's data.

claim: The long delay between HIV binding and membrane fusion may reflect a sequence of events similar to those in the model for influenza virus fusion.
source_text: We suggest that the long delay between HIV binding and membrane fusion may reflect a sequence of events similar to those in our model for influenza virus fusion.
evidence_reasoning: This is a speculative proposal extending the influenza findings to HIV.

claim: HIV fusion may require recruitment of at least a second envelope trimer, following attachment of the first.
source_text: In other words, we propose that HIV fusion may require recruitment of (at least) a second envelope trimer, following attachment of the first.
evidence_reasoning: This is a speculative hypothesis about HIV fusion mechanism.

claim: The delay time in HIV fusion would be a combination of the time needed to recruit additional envelope proteins and the time needed to activate them with CD4 and a coreceptor.
source_text: The delay time would then be a combination of the time needed to recruit one or more additional envelope proteins and the time needed to activate them with CD4 and a coreceptor.
evidence_reasoning: This is a speculative mechanistic explanation based on the proposed model.
